walkthrough: Goal: V大's 黑白灰 and his colour blocks grouped by their attributes (weeks 2 to 4): a whole picture squinted at until only its few big masses are left, each painted dark, middle or light in three greys, grouped by value and not by object (a shadow and a dark ground one mass), details left out; and the whole copy in colour blocks, the user's choice beside lines. Compare is a validated answer, never a score: the picture's masses found when its pack was built (blurred to its masses' scale, its lightness split in three by Otsu's thresholds, islands under 1 % merged) and judged by eye on the pack's contact sheet.

The pack: Import practice pack… in the practice options, the composition pack chosen in the picker: the notice says the pack is for divisions, value masses and whole copies. Stage 4's row now has four tiles in pencil: Objects, Division, Value masses (a picture's edge, its ground under the ridge tinted middle, a crown and a roof dark, a wall left light) and Whole copy.

Value masses: a drill of three compositions, the simple and medium tiers in turn, none twice, only pictures whose masses read; its How first. Title: Paint the value masses; Weeks 2 to 4 · a picture squinted at until only its few big masses are left, each dark, middle or light, grouped by value and not by object. The example, a landscape of known masses made without a pack, beside its picture, both frames its shape (S99): the darkest masses painted first in their grey (the tree's crown, wide on its right), then the light (the sky, the house and its path), the middle last over what is left; Compare: the answer's greys faint over the copy, its mass edges red, the crown's stray strip hatched in the middle grey it should be. Steps: 1 Squint: the darkest big masses with Dark, 2 Then the light ones with Light, 3 The middle last, over what is left, 4 Compare. One paragraph: a shadow and a dark ground are one mass, leave out what squinting loses, paint big, the canvas not zoomed in; Compare lays the answer's three greys over my copy as strongly as the slider sets, its mass edges red, hatched in the grey it should be where my grey differs over more than a pen's width; repaint with the same pens and compare again.

The exercise: the picture with its credit; my frame beside it is the picture's shape and size (S99), and my paint stays inside it. The tools: Dark, Middle, Light (each word underlined in its grey), Fill frame with a swatch of the grey chosen, Undo, Redo; no Sketch, Draw, Correct, wheel or eyedropper.

The biggest area first, as V大 says: Middle and Fill frame, my frame filled middle grey. Then Dark: two strokes down the tree's crown. Then Light: the sky's left half and its upper rows, the house's wall and its path; I leave the sky's right half middle. Compare: the answer's greys at half over my copy, its mass edges red as thick as the pen (the ridge, the crown, the house and path as one light mass with the wall; the roof, door and window too small to be masses), and where my grey differs over more than the grey pen's width hatching in the grey it should be: the sky's right half hatched light; the seams my light strokes left between them and along the picture's edges, the strip between them and the ridge, the crown's edges and the path's gaps, all narrower than the pen, unhatched. The card is its title and the slider Original shown, nothing else; the first Compare keeps the share of the picture at the answer's value (code 55), shown nowhere. At most of the way the answer's greys nearly cover my copy: the masses as a squinting eye sees them.

A mass repainted: with Light I paint the sky's right half (the comparison goes as my pen lands), Compare again with the slider low: the right half's hatching gone but round the crown's top, where middle is left wider than the pen; the seams between the strokes unhatched.
Next, Next: the drill's other two landscapes; Finish: Value masses drill done, its sheet small. Back in the options Value masses is inked.

Whole copy in blocks: a drill of one, its How first, its paragraph now offering colour blocks with Big, Small and Soft over the division dimmed (V大: blocks if your shapes are strong), the eyedropper comparing a point. The tools: Main, Second, Third, Draw; Big, Small, Soft and the eyedropper; Undo, Redo. I divide it in red (the ridge, the field's edge). Big: the wheel shows over the pens and Fill frame beside Undo; my division dims over a layer of colour blocks under it. A peach on the wheel, Fill frame: my frame filled; a mauve for the hills, an olive for the field, a dark green for the tree, a few strokes of Big, low completion. Compare: the picture over my copy under the slider (half at first), my division hidden. The eyedropper on the path in my copy (painted olive, the path left out): both colours on the wheel and in the colour table under the slider, my block darker by 19 ΔE, nearly all of it lightness. Finish: Whole copy drill done.

With the pack, Stage 4 · Simplifying starts stage 4's first session: after a warm-up of the kinds met (none: these never warm up), three objects, a division and then value masses (in the first, third, fifth sessions; a whole copy in the others, as s95's second session shows), about 29 to 31 minutes; Next past the objects and the division: Value masses 1 of 1, its How by itself (a session's sheet reads its stage's sessions, not drills), an upright medium picture.
